headline: Persian Gulf oil exports 'surpassed pre-conflict levels' (X post Oct 23, now carried by ANI wire) -- direct clash with counted
dek: Bessent: 'Despite Iran's efforts to disrupt energy shipments, oil exports from the Persian Gulf are roaring back and have surpassed pre-conflict levels. The message is clear: Iran's threats have failed to stop the flow of energy to global markets.' Previously held at 1000-06 as single-family…
sources: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (X post, Oct 23, 2026); ANI wire carry via Tribune India / Economic Times (Oct 24)
fault_line: Who is telling the truth about the Gulf's oil: Washington says exports beat pre-war levels, the counted ships say traffic collapsed -- is the oil flowing, or is the blockade story?

sections.what_happened: Bessent: 'Despite Iran's efforts to disrupt energy shipments, oil exports from the Persian Gulf are roaring back and have surpassed pre-conflict levels. The message is clear: Iran's threats have failed to stop the flow of energy to global markets.' Previously held at 1000-06 as single-family (Economic Times only); this scan adds ANI as a second, T1 wire family carrying the identical X quote, plus Bessent's own post as primary source.
sections.what_verified: Quote itself confirmed by two families: Bessent's own X post (primary) + ANI wire carry (Tribune India, Economic Times, Desi Talk Chicago all carrying the same ANI text = 1 wire family). The UNDERLYING export figure is NOT independently verified: no export-volume dataset is cited in any carry, and it sits in direct tension with IMF PortWatch counted transits (see counterevidence).
sections.what_disputed: IMF PortWatch (snapshot 2026-10-23, fetched 23:47 ): counted 4 total transits through Hormuz on 2026-10-18 (2 tankers), 7-day average 3.71 vs calendar-2025 baseline 85.53/day (4.3%). CAUTION: the snapshot is now STALE by the >5-day rule (observation 6 days old at this scan; flag was false at Oct 23 fetch when lag was 5 days) -- cite only with the Oct 18 date and the stale warning, never as a live figure. Exports and transits are different metrics (cargo volumes vs vessel counts), so the clash is a narrative clash, not a disproof -- but no dataset in any Bessent carry supports 'surpassed pre-conflict levels'. Social echo '82% of normal traffic' (flagged 1000-06) remains unattributed misinformation-grade and is NOT adopted.
sections.why_matters: Two numbers, one strait: Washington claims Gulf oil exports beat pre-war levels. The counted ships tell the opposite story. The number that decides it is dated Oct 18 -- and it is already stale.
sections.context: Background: UPGRADE of totw-20261024-1000-06 (was single-family HOLD) -- Bessent: Persian Gulf oil exports 'surpassed pre-conflict levels' (X post Oct 23, now carried by ANI wire) -- direct clash with counted Hormuz transits (Hormuz by the Numbers franchise)

The number that decides it is dated Oct 18 -- and it is already stale.
